Inspect and repair the boot firmware of a VM.

```text
pomme firmware SUBCOMMAND
```

## pomme firmware inspect

Show a VM's boot firmware and whether a guest update left the VM short of memory.

Pomme reads the firmware from the auxiliary storage of the VM, so this works while the VM is stopped. While the VM runs normal macOS with a connected Pomme agent, Pomme also asks the guest for its macOS version and usable memory, and bases the diagnosis on them. The diagnosis is `affected`, `likely-affected`, `not-affected`, or `unknown`.

```text
pomme firmware inspect [NAMES ...] [--json] [--format FORMAT] [--debug] [--progress PROGRESS]
```

| Argument | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `NAMES` | VM names. Uses `POMME_VM_NAME` when omitted. |

This command also accepts the [common flags](/reference/cli/#common-flags).

## pomme firmware repair

Restore the boot firmware that a VM was installed with.

Use this when `pomme firmware inspect` reports `incompatible-update` for a VM that runs macOS 26 or earlier: a guest update to macOS 26.7 or 15.8 installed the macOS 27 boot firmware, which leaves the guest about 1.75 GB of memory. The VM must be stopped. Pomme saves a copy of the `AuxiliaryStorage` file in the `FirmwareBackups` folder of the VM bundle, then copies the firmware that the VM was installed with over the firmware that the update installed. When the firmware needs no repair, Pomme changes nothing. Never use it on a VM that you upgraded to macOS 27 in the guest.

```text
pomme firmware repair [NAME] [--force] [--json] [--format FORMAT] [--debug] [--progress PROGRESS]
```

| Argument | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `NAME` | VM name. Uses `POMME_VM_NAME` when omitted. |

| Flag | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `-f`, `--force` | Repair without prompting. |

This command also accepts the [common flags](/reference/cli/#common-flags).
